bills.title: AI Content Provenance Requirements
bills.summary: Would require generative AI providers to embed provenance data in any video, image, or audio content that is created or materially altered by their generative AI system. Additionally, the generative AI provider is required to include in the provenance data any information that relates to a reasonably identifiable individual.
bills.status_detail: Passed first chamber

bills.title: AI Transparency, Employment Anti-Bias, and Chatbot Safety Act
bills.summary: Introduced by the General Law Committee, this bill would implement transparency and anti-bias measures in automated employment-related decision processes. The bill would also require providers of AI companions to include protocols for detecting harmful content and restrict minors' interactions with those AI companions. The bill also requires AI-generated content to be clearly marked and detectable. A public hearing on the bill was held during the week of March 5.
bills.status_detail: Public hearing held in General Law Committee during week of March 5, 2026

bills.title: Florida AI Bill of Rights and Chatbot Disclosure Act
bills.summary: AI Bill of Rights which would provide citizens certain AI rights, such as the right to limit control of minors' access to AI or know if AI companies are collecting personal information, as well as requiring notice for chatbots.
bills.status_detail: Passed Senate; House Speaker indicated he will not bring the bill to the House Floor this session, citing the White House's position on state AI regulation

bills.title: Generative AI Product Liability for Minors
bills.summary: Would classify generative AI systems as personal property for product liability cases involving minors, establishes liability for product sellers, and imposes a duty to warn of risks.
bills.status_detail: Passed committee

bills.title: Chatbot Data Minimization and Restrictions Act
bills.summary: Would implement strict data minimization requirements for chatbot providers, prohibit using chat logs for advertising purposes, and prohibit chatbots from providing medical, legal, or financial advice.
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: AI Transcription Consent for Healthcare Visits
bills.summary: Would require healthcare professionals to obtain a patient's verbal consent before utilizing AI transcription services during medical visits.
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: AI Notice and Employment Decision Restrictions
bills.summary: Would require employers to provide clear notice to job applicants when AI is used and prohibit using solely automated decision-making tools for discipline, termination, or deactivation decisions.
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: Mississippi Artificial Intelligence Definition Act
bills.summary: Would add a definition of 'artificial intelligence' to Mississippi code, largely modeled on the OECD's AI definition.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; sent to Governor, who has until March 9, 2026 to sign

bills.title: AI Chatbot Safety and Age Verification for Minors
bills.summary: Would prohibit AI chatbots from offering features deemed unsafe for minors and would require age verification.
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: Chatbot Age Restrictions and Therapeutic Chatbot Requirements
bills.summary: Would prohibit chatbots from being made available to minors if they have human-like features and would require the implementation of reasonable age-verification systems, with additional requirements for therapeutic chatbots.
bills.status_detail: Passed committee

bills.title: Civil Liability for AI-Caused Harm
bills.summary: Would establish a civil cause of action for injuries caused by AI, holding developers strictly liable for those harms.
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: High-Risk AI System Reasonable Care Requirements
bills.summary: Would require developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to implement reasonable care to protect against foreseeable risks, including by adhering to recognized frameworks like NIST's AI RMF or ISO standards.
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: Utah AI Regulatory Sandbox Expansion
bills.summary: Amends Utah's existing regulatory sandbox (SB 149, 2024) by expanding the program, allowing applicants to apply for a regulatory mitigation agreement or a joint interpretation agreement clarifying the application of state law to AI. Directs the Office of AI Policy to perform regular audits of participants while agreements are in effect and allows up to two extensions. Also makes amendments to Utah's Artificial Intelligence Learning Laboratory Program.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; sent to Governor

bills.title: Utah Automated Decision Making and Privacy Framework Update
bills.summary: Would update Utah's data privacy laws by introducing new definitions for automated decision making and profiling, including requiring the development of a data privacy framework that incorporates best practices for automated decision making. The bill defines automated decision making as 'using personal data to make a decision about an individual through automated processing, without human review or intervention,' a narrower definition than California's CCPA regulations.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; awaiting amendment concurrence

bills.title: Utah Digital Content Provenance and AI Disclosure Act
bills.summary: Would require large online platforms (over 2 million monthly users) to detect, disclose, and preserve digital provenance data in distributed content and provide users with tools to inspect that information. Would also require generative AI providers (over 1 million monthly users) to embed latent disclosures in AI-generated or substantially modified content, and require device manufacturers to embed similar disclosures in content captured by devices sold after January 1, 2028. The Division of Consumer Protection would enforce and could impose administrative fines. Also includes new protections and takedown procedures addressing non-consensual AI-generated intimate images.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; awaiting amendment concurrence

bills.title: Education Technology Regulatory Sandbox for AI Tools
bills.summary: Would establish an Education Technology Regulatory Sandbox for public education, allowing three-year pilot programs for testing AI tools under defined safety, privacy, and oversight requirements. Approved pilots would require human-in-the-loop educator supervision, parental notice and opt-out rights, student data protections, safety testing, and evaluation of educational outcomes. Vendors must conduct annual red teaming exercises that test system responses to harmful requests that minors might reasonably make. Follows SB 149 (2024).
bills.status_detail: Passed first chamber

bills.title: Future of AI Innovation Act
bills.summary: Aimed at strengthening U.S. leadership in AI research and standards development. Would formally authorize NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) to develop voluntary AI standards, benchmarks, and evaluation frameworks in collaboration with industry and federal agencies. Would establish public-private AI testbeds with national laboratories to evaluate AI systems, support research in advanced manufacturing, robotics, and quantum technologies, create AI grand challenge prize competitions, expand access to federal datasets for AI research, and promote international collaboration on AI standards and R&D.
bills.status_detail: Reintroduced by Senators Young (R-IN) and Cantwell (D-WA)

bills.title: Alabama Biological and Neural Data Protection Act
bills.summary: Would prohibit the disclosure of biological data (data generated by measurement of an individual's biological, genetic, biochemical, physiological, or neural properties used for identification purposes) or neural data without a consumer's consent. Amended to apply only to owners or operators of a health and fitness application.
bills.status_detail: Passed House

bills.title: Louisiana Comprehensive Privacy Act (Virginia-Style)
bills.summary: A Virginia-style comprehensive consumer data privacy bill with the broader definition of sale ('or other valuable consideration').
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: Maine Comprehensive Privacy Act (Maryland-Style)
bills.summary: A Maryland-style comprehensive privacy bill. The Maine Senate voted to adopt Committee Amendment 'A' on LD 1822, as well as an amendment to that amendment. Key changes in the Senate floor amendment include: expanding the definition of 'publicly available information'; adding an exemption for political organizations; and delaying the effective date to September 1, 2027. The bill's second reading is scheduled for the next legislative day. If the bill passes the Senate, it will need to be reconciled with the House version.
bills.status_detail: Senate voted to adopt Committee Amendment A and floor amendment; second reading scheduled for next legislative day

bills.title: Oregon Public Body Data Broker Disclosure Restrictions
bills.summary: Would prohibit a public body from disclosing personally identifiable information to a data broker unless the data broker first provides a written attestation that the information will not be sold or otherwise transferred to any entity that will use the information to enforce federal immigration law. Bill has been passed by the legislature but not yet transmitted to the governor.
bills.status_detail: Legislature passed; pending transmission to governor for signature

bills.title: South Dakota Direct-to-Consumer Genetic Privacy Act
bills.summary: A direct-to-consumer genetic privacy bill. The House passed it on March 4, 2026. This bill previously passed the Senate but will require a concurrence vote after being amended in a House committee.
bills.status_detail: House passed on March 4, 2026; requires Senate concurrence vote on House amendment

bills.title: Virginia VCDPA Amendment: Prohibition on Geolocation Data Sale
bills.summary: Would amend the Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act (VCDPA) to prohibit a controller from selling or offering for sale precise geolocation data concerning a consumer. The bill will head to Governor Spanberger (D) to sign or veto.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers of the legislature; pending signature or veto by Governor Spanberger (D)

bills.title: Virginia Consumer Protection Act: Reproductive Health Data GLBA Exception
bills.summary: A proposed amendment to the Virginia Consumer Protection Act. If signed by Governor Spanberger, this bill will add a GLBA data-level exception to the consent requirement for obtaining, disclosing, selling, or disseminating personally identifiable reproductive or sexual health information.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers of the legislature; pending signature or veto by Governor Spanberger (D)

bills.title: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0)
bills.summary: COPPA 2.0. The Senate voted to pass COPPA 2.0 by unanimous consent on March 5, 2026. The House Energy and Commerce Committee was simultaneously conducting a markup hearing on its own version of COPPA 2.0, which it later tabled, with Chairman Guthrie stating both sides had made 'substantial progress' towards bipartisan support and the bill would be held for continued negotiation.
bills.status_detail: Senate passed by unanimous consent on March 5, 2026; House version tabled by House Energy and Commerce Committee pending continued negotiation

bills.title: Kids Internet and Digital Safety (KIDS) Act
bills.summary: An omnibus bill combining 12 separate proposals from the youth online privacy and safety bill package introduced in November, including the SCREEN Act, KOSA, the Safe Messaging for Kids Act, the SPY Kids Act, the Safer GAMING Act, and the SAFE Bots Act. The SAFE Bots Act component would regulate consumer-facing AI chatbots interacting with minors: prohibiting chatbots from falsely claiming to be licensed professionals, requiring disclosures confirming the chatbot is not human, requiring crisis resource disclosures when users express suicidal ideation, and requiring 'take a break' disclosures after three hours of continuous interaction. A committee amendment changes KOSA's preemption language, clarifying that broadly applicable preemption would not preclude state laws on contracts, torts, product liability, consumer protection, or criminal law. The bill would preempt some conflicting state chatbot laws (e.g., California's SB 243 and New York's S-3008C).
bills.status_detail: Amended and reported out of House Energy and Commerce Committee; amendment adopted as amendment in the nature of a substitute (AINS) from Rep. Guthrie (R-KY)

bills.title: Sammy's Law: Parental Monitoring Obligations for Social Media
bills.summary: Would impose parental monitoring obligations on large social media platform providers, requiring them to make available APIs allowing third-party safety software providers to manage children's interactions, content, and account settings under a parent or guardian's delegation. Amendment changes include: extending the timeline for creating the third-party-accessible real-time API from 30 days to 180 days after the effective date; expanding data minimization and data security obligations; adding protections for encrypted messages; and prohibiting third-party safety software providers from selling user data.
bills.status_detail: Amended and reported out of House Energy and Commerce Committee; amendment sponsored by Rep. Carter (R-GA)

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: Would establish a system of user age verification and parental consent for minors at the app store level, similar to laws enacted in Texas, Utah, Louisiana, and Alabama. Key amendment changes include: extending age verification and parental consent requirements to existing accounts; requiring parental consent for pre-installed apps; adopting a definition for 'in-app purchases'; allowing developers to request app store providers prevent minor app downloads; and adding language permitting developers to rely on alternative age category information if there is 'clear and convincing' evidence it is more accurate. Includes judicial review language restricting constitutional challenges to the DC District Court within 60 days of enactment.
bills.status_detail: Amended and reported out of House Energy and Commerce Committee; amendment sponsored by Rep. James (R-MI)
